newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU ministers to take boats, cars to reach Libya.
newsitem.headline: OAU ministers to take boats, cars to reach Libya.

text.p: African foreign ministers will travel to sanctions-hit Libya by road and sea next month for an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) meeting.

"They will travel to Tripoli by road from Tunisia and by boat from Malta to attend the annual ministerial conference from February 24 to 28," Mamadou Ba, head of the OAU's political department, told Reuters on Monday.
OAU sources said it would be the pan-African body's highest-level meeting in Libya since an inquorate summit in 1982.

A U.N. air embargo was slapped on Libya for refusing to turn over to the United States or Britain two suspects in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland, in which 270 people were killed.
"Because of the U.N. air sanctions the African foreign ministers will not be able to fly direct to Tripoli," Ba said.
Libya argues that the two suspects, both Libyan nationals, would not get a fair trial in the United States or Britain and wants them tried at a neutral venue, a position supported by the OAU.

OAU sources said Libya was expected to highlight the sufferings of its people as a result of the air embargo, taking ministers to hospitals without medicines and factories closed due to a lack of spare parts and raw materials.
Ba said the foreign ministers, preparing for next June's annual OAU summit in Zimbabwe, would discuss African conflicts in eastern Zaire, Burundi, Sudan, Somalia and Liberia.
